newsitem.title: CONGO: Mobutu clan gathers in Congo for flight into exile.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu clan gathers in Congo for flight into exile.

text.p: About 30 members of ousted President Mobutu Sese Seko's close family gathered in Congo on Saturday to await a flight into exile after rebels moved into Zaire's capital Kinshasa, witnesses said.

Officials at Brazzaville's airport said Mobutu's soldier son, Mobutu Kongolo, and the commander of the feared presidential guard, General Nzimbi Ngbale, were among those waiting to board the presidential jet.
Other members of the party included their families and some of those who profited most from Mobutu's three decades rule over Africa's third largest nation.
"The ultimate destination is Morocco but there is some question that they will stop at Gbadolite on the way," one airport official told Reuters.
Mobutu, fighting cancer and a seven-month civil war, slipped out of Kinshasa quietly on Friday and travelled to his northern jungle palace in his ancestral home district of Gbadolite.
Laurent Kabila's rebels moved into Kinshasa on Saturday.
Mobutu, 66, seized power in 1965 and proved one of the continent's most enduring strongmen. Western powers supported him as a Cold War bastion against Soviet communism.

Denounced as everything from a dictator to a thief, critics say he plundered what is potentially one of Africa's richest countries and amassed a huge personal fortune while his people struggled against poverty and neglect.
Characteristically defiant, Mobutu refused to resign as head of state, as demanded by Kabila, but his abrupt departure triggered intense speculation that he was on his way to exile.
In Morocco, officials said Mobutu and his family were expected to arrive in Rabat on Saturday night and stay in a hotel about 20 km (13 miles) to the south of the city on the Atlantic coast.

A Reuters correspondent saw unusual deployment of security forces around the Amphitrite hotel. "The hotel was booked for Mobutu and his family... Therefore it is now not open to the public," one Moroccan official said.
As the Mobutu clan waited at the airport, Kabila's rebels moved to consolidate their hold over Mobutu's former capital -- just five km (three miles) across the river from Brazzaville.
Kongolo, an officer in the presidential guard, fled Kinshasa on Saturday in a speed boat with 20 other men.
Nzimbi, who has close family ties to Mobutu, fled on Friday.

Nzimbi commanded the Special Presidential Division (DSP), the most disciplined, best-paid and professional of Zaire's fighting forces. Their duty was to ensure Mobutu's personal security and defend vital national interests.
Most presidential guards came from Mobutu's Ngbandi tribe.
Witnesses and diplomats in Kinshasa, spoke of a drive by hardline Mobutu supporters to kill members of his last government suspected of trying to appease the rebels or of giving up the fight.

Diplomats said presidential guards had killed defence minister and army chief of staff General Mahele Lieko Bokungo. Mahele, killed in Kinshasa on Friday night, had been planning to meet Kabila to discuss handing over power, they added.
Diplomats said they feared foreign minister Kamanda wa Kamanda had been shot dead on Saturday by one of his bodyguards for similar reasons. There was no confirmation of that report.
